# Harness Summary

The candidate achieves moderate eval accuracy (64.6% on ds_alpha, 72.9% on ds_beta, ds_gamma incomplete) but exhibits strong **label frequency bias**, repeatedly predicting the same high-frequency labels regardless of input content. A critical pattern is weak demonstration utilization—the reasoning outputs are generic ("Closest demonstrations suggest X") without explaining feature alignment, indicating the harness fails to extract meaningful distinctions between labels or properly ground its predictions. Training accuracy is unexpectedly lower than eval accuracy in ds_alpha (42.9% vs 64.6%), suggesting either the training distribution is harder or the online learning mechanism isn't effectively accumulating knowledge. The prompts maintain ~2KB of context through in-context examples but show no evidence of learning task-specific word associations to disambiguate a crowded label space (14+ classes). To improve, focus on (1) making demonstrations more contrastive/distinctive, (2) adding explicit feature extraction guidance in the prompt, and (3) investigating the anomalous train/eval accuracy inversion.
